newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian police detain 43 after Timor protest.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian police detain 43 after Timor protest.

text.p: Indonesian police detained 43 youths on Sunday after an "anti-integration" demonstration outside a hotel in the East Timor capital of Dili where a United Nations envoy was staying, police said.

"There was a demonstration outside the Mahkota hotel where the envoy was staying," East Timor deputy police chief Colonel Atok Rismanto told Reuters by telephone from Dili. "Forty-three people were detained," he said.

Rismanto said the demonstrators, numbering about 100, opposed integration with Indonesia. He said several were injured by broken glass from the hotel's windows but provided no other details on the 7 a.m. incident.
The U.N. special envoy on East Timor, Jamsheed Marker, arrived in East Timor on Friday to meet with senior government and community leaders in the former Portuguese colony.
Rismanto said police quickly dispersed the protesters and Marker, who was inside the hotel at the time, was able to leave on a scheduled helicopter tour of several districts in the territory.
Those detained were being questioned and police were looking for others involved in the incident, he said.

East Timor was invaded by Indonesia in 1975 after the abrupt withdrawal of Portuguese colonial authorities. It was annexed by Indonesia the following year in a move not recognised by the United Nations and its status is disputed.
